statement: The pie chart shows how the 120 pupils of a school travel there. The angle for the bus is not marked. How many more pupils come by bus than by bike?

figure.alt: A pie chart with four sectors. Going clockwise from the top: Walk, marked 105 degrees; Bus, with no angle marked; Car, marked 75 degrees; Bike, marked 45 degrees.

choices.misconception: I found the difference between the bus and bike angles in degrees and gave that, as if each degree were one pupil.
I found how many pupils come by bus but did not subtract the bike pupils.
I saw the difference was a quarter of the circle and gave 25, thinking of 25 percent.
I found how many pupils come by bike and stopped there.

hints: The four angles of a pie chart add up to 360 degrees.
First find the bus angle from the other three. Then turn angles into pupils: the whole 360 degrees stands for 120 pupils, so work out how many degrees stand for one pupil.
The bus angle is 360 - 105 - 75 - 45 = 135 degrees. Each pupil is 3 degrees.

solutions.reliable: The angles add up to 360 degrees, so the bus angle is 360 - 105 - 75 - 45 = 135 degrees. The 120 pupils fill 360 degrees, so each pupil is 3 degrees. Bus: 135 / 3 = 45 pupils. Bike: 45 / 3 = 15 pupils. The difference is 45 - 15 = 30 pupils. The transferable idea: a pie chart shows fractions of a whole, so convert angles to a fraction of 360 before converting to people.
solutions.elegant: The difference in angle is 135 - 45 = 90 degrees, a quarter of the circle, and a quarter of 120 pupils is 30.

whyOnTest: Reading a pie chart: find a missing angle from the 360-degree total, then turn an angle difference into a number of people.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
